result:
Rebase on a shared branch rarely. It rewrites history, so anyone who already pulled the old commits gets diverged branches and forced-push pain.

Use rebase only when:
- Only you have commits on the branch, or the team agreed to it beforehand.
- You rebase local, unpushed commits onto the updated base (`git pull --rebase`) to avoid noisy merge commits.
- You clean up your own commits (squash, reword) before the branch is shared or merged.

Use merge when:
- Others have pulled or based work on the branch.
- You want to preserve true history without force-pushing.

Rule: never rebase commits others already have. If you must, use `git push --force-with-lease` and warn the team first.
